public_rationale: Research published in 2020 documented both hallucinated content and basic reasoning failures. That supports the ordinary historical claim that these reliability problems were not new in December 2025. It does not establish that they are inevitable or unchanged.
limitations: The evidence establishes continuity in broad failure categories, not identical causes across model generations.
It does not assess Marcus's separate claim that world models are necessary for reliability.

statement.excerpt: The technical problems are not new.
statement.document_title: The AI bubble is all over now, baby blue

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that factual unreliability and failures of reasoning were documented years before this post.
The historical comparison includes the period beginning in 2019 mentioned in the surrounding text. It does not require every current failure to have been identified in 2019.
This claim concerns the age of the problems, not whether they are permanent or whether performance has improved.
criteria.support_condition: Dated research from years before publication documents hallucinations and reasoning failures in large language models or their direct predecessors.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Historical records establish that the relevant problems first appeared near publication and were materially different from earlier documented failures.
